title: Polaris Security & Networking Discovery - Redwood Private/VPC
next_steps: Send network diagram template and Redwood Private VPC runbook
Share SOC2/ISO audit excerpts and KMS integration guide
Schedule follow-up technical deep-dive with Raj and Samir for week of 11/15
Provision trial Dedicated capacity for 2-week benchmark
action_items: Maya: email network diagram template and security pack by 2027-11-07
Liam: prepare POC checklist and estimated sizing by 2027-11-10
Samir: share current VPC peering topology and CIDR ranges by 2027-11-08
summary: Intro discovery focused on private VPC deployment. Customer constraints: strict egress controls, prefer VPC endpoints over peering for auditability, multi-region failover requirement, and KMS/HSM integration. Agreed to send network runbook and security docs and schedule a deep technical session.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya from Redwood, AE on the account. Liam our SE is with me. quick roll call?
[00:10] Raj Patel: Raj here, head of infra at Polaris. Elena on security, Samir on cloud, Tina product.
[00:15] Maya Chen: Great, glad to have you. objective today is to understand your networking and security constraints for Redwood Private / VPC option. we'll cover peering, endpoints, regions, and KMS.
[00:25] Liam O'Neill: Hi! quick small intro on Redwood Private - it's basically a customer-dedicated control plane with private networking options, supports VPC peering, AWS PrivateLink endpoints, and can be deployed in your VPC or via our managed private carriers. sorry, Privat sometimes in notes, typos.
[00:40] Elena Korhonen: Important to flag up front: Polaris requires zero public egress from production inference services. every outbound must go through approved egress proxies and we need per-request audit logs.
[00:50] Samir Khan: yeah and ephemeral keys are a requirement; we use CloudHSM for key storage and KMS for lifecycle. also, we want regional isolation for EU and NA data residency.
[01:05] Maya Chen: Understood. quick question on traffic flows — do you prefer VPC peering (direct routing) or PrivateLink / interface endpoints?
[01:15] Raj Patel: Preference right now is PrivateLink because peering creates a lot of transitive routing concerns across our account boundaries. we have many shared services and peering creates route table complexity.
[01:25] Liam O'Neill: PrivateLink makes sense for auditability; you get an elastic network interface in your subnet. caveat: PrivateLink requires us to host the NLB/endpoint service in a region where your VPC exists.
[01:35] Tina Morales: if we do PrivateLink does that affect latency much for real-time inference? our SLAs target p95 generation latency under 200ms for single-turn prompts.
[01:45] Liam O'Neill: Typical added overhead from PrivateLink is small — single-digit ms — but depends on region and path. for strict 200ms p95 it's feasible; we recommend a pilot to measure. Also, model size and batch settings matter.
[01:58] Elena Korhonen: On compliance we need attestations: SOC2, ISO 27001 sections about network segregation, and proof of KMS integration. do you support CloudHSM or customer-managed keys?
[02:10] Maya Chen: Yes, Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations. we can integrate with AWS CloudHSM and customer KMS keys, and we provide audit logs for all encryption key operations. we'll send the KMS integration guide.
[02:25] Raj Patel: Another ask: we don't want any egress to non-approved IP ranges. can Redwood restrict egress to our proxy endpoints?
[02:35] Liam O'Neill: We support egress control via route tables and security groups in your VPC — for Redwood-hosted components that require outbound, we can front them behind an interface endpoint to your proxy. for hosted control plane calls, in private deployment mode the control plane traffic traverses the private connection; no public internet needed.
[02:50] Samir Khan: We use strict NACLs and have a managed NAT instance policy — ideally 0 public subnets for inference. how does Redwood handle NAT or internet access for things like container image pulls and OS patches?
[03:05] Priya Desai: good question. for private deployments we offer two models: 1) customer-managed image repo and patch mirrors inside your VPC so no public egress needed; 2) if you want Redwood to manage updates we can do it through an approved egress path you provide — still a private peering/endpoint. Both approaches are used in enterprise deployments.
[03:25] Raj Patel: We like option (1). we already have an internal artifact repo. can Redwood pull from our repo over PrivateLink?
[03:33] Liam O'Neill: yes, we can pull over an interface endpoint in your VPC. we'll need the service endpoints and permissions set up. we'll include a checklist.
[03:40] Elena Korhonen: about regions: Polaris needs EU data to stay within eu-west-1 and eu-central-1. if we deploy Redwood in those regions, do you support multi-region failover without cross-region replication of raw logs?
[03:55] Maya Chen: We support region-local deployments. for multi-region failover we can either: a) replicate model artifacts only and keep logs in-region, or b) failover to a secondary region with ephemeral replication of the minimal state needed. we can configure logs to stay in-region for compliance.
[04:15] Tina Morales: so if a region goes down can we failover traffic to NA? that would be a last resort and we'd need approvals.
[04:22] Liam O'Neill: yes, can be done but requires agreement on data movement controls. recommend a canary failover plan with explicit push-button process.
[04:30] Raj Patel: networking specifics — do you require overlapping CIDRs? we plan to use 10.0.0.0/16 across primary acct and 10.1.0.0/16 for dev, etc.
[04:40] Liam O'Neill: overlapping CIDRs are a problem for peering. PrivateLink avoids that since it's an ENI-based connection. for peering you'd need non-overlapping ranges. we'll send guidance.
[04:50] Samir Khan: latency to consider if we place Redwood endpoints in eu-central-1 — our users are largely EU; what about capacity sizing?
[05:00] Maya Chen: for sizing we'll need your QPS, typical sequence lengths, model family. we can propose Dedicated pools sized to hit your p95 targets. Liam will put together an estimate based on your workloads.
[05:12] Elena Korhonen: security logging: do you produce request-level logs with identifiers but sanitized PII? we need to map logs to SSO identities and have immutable audit trails.
[05:25] Priya Desai: Redwood can emit structured audit logs to your CloudWatch/Stackdriver or S3 endpoint. logs can include request IDs, user IDs (mapped from your SSO), latency, model/version, but we also have tooling to scrub or obfuscate PII before storage if needed.
[05:45] Raj Patel: we use Okta SAML for SSO and expect RBAC provisioning via SCIM. can Redwood tie to our IdP?
[05:55] Maya Chen: yes, we support SAML SSO and SCIM-based provisioning for RBAC. in Private mode, SSO flows are internal to your network.
[06:05] Samir Khan: curious about how secrets get injected — does Redwood store credentials in its control plane or do we provide them via Secrets Manager?
[06:15] Liam O'Neill: we prefer customers to manage secrets in their KMS/Secrets Manager and pass them via the private link or our secure secret sync mechanism that stores only encrypted blobs in the control plane. for Private deployments, control plane can be customer-hosted so keys never leave your environment.
[06:35] Elena Korhonen: incident response — we need playbooks, runbooks, and support for SIEM forwarding. do you have predefined integrations?
[06:45] Maya Chen: yes, we have SIEM integrations and can forward logs via HTTPS endpoints and SNS/SQS. we'll share a runbook and existing SOC escalation matrix.
[06:55] Tina Morales: procurement question — timeline if we choose Dedicated or Private? we have board review in Q1.
[07:03] Maya Chen: typical timeline for Private deployment is 6-8 weeks after network and security review and PO. Dedicated reserved capacity can be faster if it's hosted. we'll work to align on your board timeline.
[07:12] Raj Patel: what about maintenance windows and change control? we need blackout windows and advance notice for kernel updates.
[07:20] Priya Desai: we support scheduled maintenance windows and can coordinate in your change control. we also support rolling updates to avoid downtime.
[07:30] Samir Khan: does Redwood require a transit gateway for multi-account access? we have multiple AWS accounts and use TGW for shared services.
[07:40] Liam O'Neill: We can integrate with AWS Transit Gateway. often customers present two patterns: a) service endpoints per account via PrivateLink, or b) central Transit Gateway with peering to Redwood's management VPC. PrivateLink plus TGW is common when you want central egress and shared services.
[07:55] Elena Korhonen: encryption in transit — TLS mutual auth?
[08:00] Liam O'Neill: mutual TLS is supported for service-to-service; we also support mTLS for control plane and client connections where required.
[08:10] Raj Patel: we need pen test reports and third-party attestations.
[08:15] Maya Chen: we'll provide the latest pen test summary and third-party certs. some redacted items but enough for your security review.
[08:25] Tina Morales: regarding cost, do you charge extra for PrivateLink endpoints or TGW?
[08:30] Maya Chen: Cost model: Private has platform fee plus infra usage. PrivateLink/TGW egress charges are passed through; we'll include ballpark. recommended to run a small POC to quantify.
[08:40] Samir Khan: POC idea: run 2 models — a small 7B open model and a 70B family model — measure latency, throughput, and cost for 2 weeks.
[08:50] Liam O'Neill: sounds good. we'll create a POC checklist: network setup, credentials, sample traffic, success metrics (p95 latency <200ms, throughput X rps).
[09:00] Elena Korhonen: can we insist on logs being write-once and retained for 1 year in-region?
[09:07] Priya Desai: yes retention policies are configurable; write-once semantics can be implemented via S3 object lock if you host logs in your S3. We'll document the options.
[09:17] Raj Patel: for the initial setup who do you need from our side?
[09:21] Maya Chen: network owner (Samir), security (Elena), and an application owner (Tina) for success criteria. plus a technical deep-dive with Liam to go over VPC flow.
[09:32] Samir Khan: i'll pull current network diagrams and CIDR lists and send them.
[09:36] Maya Chen: great. we'll follow up with the runbook, SOC docs, and a proposed POC plan. schedule a technical deep-dive for the week of 11/15?
[09:45] Raj Patel: yes that works.
[09:48] Tina Morales: quick Q — does Redwood support egress policies to block model telemetry leaving our accounts? we want usage metrics but not raw request data externally.
[09:58] Liam O'Neill: telemetry can be routed to your telemetry endpoints only; we can redact or aggregate request content before it leaves. default is to keep telemetry in your environment for Private.
[10:10] Elena Korhonen: any known limitations with Azure or GCP for PrivateLink-equivalents?
[10:15] Liam O'Neill: AWS PrivateLink is our most mature path. on GCP we leverage VPC Service Controls and Serverless VPC Access; on Azure we use Private Endpoints. feature parity is close but small differences exist in setup. we'll include cloud-specific runbooks.
[10:30] Raj Patel: last thing, what's the rollback plan if we see a regression after a model rollout?
[10:35] Priya Desai: we have model rollout features: A/B and canary traffic split with automatic fallback. rollbacks are quick and routable via the routing rules in the control plane. for Private we replicate the same controls.
[10:48] Maya Chen: ok wrapping up. recap: 1) Maya to send network template, SOC docs, KMS guide. 2) Liam to produce POC checklist and sizing. 3) Samir to share network diagram and CIDRs. 4) schedule tech deep-dive wk of 11/15. any other items?
[11:05] Raj Patel: no, that's it. thanks.
[11:10] Elena Korhonen: thanks all.
[11:12] Maya Chen: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the docs and a calendar invite. bye.
[44:50] End of Recording.
